scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The hyporchema originated among the Dorians, likely in Crete, as part of their musical and poetic traditions.
It was introduced early to Delos, where it was performed at Apollo's festivals and persisted until at least the 2nd century CE, as noted by Lucian.
It was a lyric dance combining song and mimicry, evolving into playful and comic forms.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The hyporchema was performed during Apollo's worship festivals, serving as a ritual expression combining music, dance, and poetry.
Its playful and comic aspects linked it to communal celebration and religious devotion.
The related geranos dance symbolized the labyrinth and Theseus' mythic journey, suggesting a ritual dimension of myth reenactment.
Today it is a living tradition.
